title: Sprint Zero: Infer elevator, demo script, and pricing frames
content:
Context and goal:
This is a compact "Sprint Zero" messaging kit for the Hosted API that balances three things for early technical buyers: 1) a 30s engineer-friendly elevator, 2) a 90s demo script that an AE or solution engineer can run, and 3) recommended pricing language for product pages, in-console tooltips, and first outreach (email/Slack).

Why this is different (framing):
- Developer-first means we speak in engineering outcomes (latency, reproducibility, cost controls) not just features.
- The quickstart promise should reduce time-to-first-value: measurable inference returned from a real workload in minutes, with explicit guardrails so teams don’t get surprised on cost.
- Pricing language needs to be honest + operational: per-token units for power users, example cost calculators for PMs, and committed/discount language for platform buyers.

30-second elevator (engineer-focused):
"Redwood Hosted API gives your app production-quality LLM inference without the ops — predictable latency, automatic batching and prefix caching to cut token cost, and a single API that runs the same in hosted, dedicated, or private environments. Ship features fast, calibrate quality at the prompt set level, and keep costs under control with per-route quotas, autoscaling, and simple per-1k token pricing."

90-second demo script (for AE / SE):
- Setup (0–30s): "We’ll show you a full flow — from sign-up to a sample inference in under 5 minutes. I’ll paste a short prompt and call the API."
- Run (30–75s): Execute a single request (show code snippet in console). Point out streaming response, latency metric, and tokens used.
- Operational follow-up (75–90s): Show route dashboard: token breakdown, tail-latency, and how to pin a model version or enable a fallback model. End with: "If you like this, we can spin a dedicated pool or setup a private VPC for predictable throughput."

Engineer persona microcopy (three tones):
- Minimal/short: "Same API, better economics — low-latency inference with caching and per-route cost controls."
- Explicit/technical: "Prefix KV caching, continuous batching, and model-variant fallback reduce per-token cost while keeping 99th % latency within your SLOs."
- Product/PM friendly: "Deploy a model in minutes, see token and latency costs per route, and scale with reserved capacity when you’re ready."

Objections + quick rebuttals (seismic buyer questions):
- "How do you keep costs down compared to hosted endpoints?" -> "Two levers: runtime-level savings (prefix/KV caching + intelligent batching) and product-level controls (per-route quotas, autoscaling policies, and quantization profiles). We show token breakdowns so you can tune."
- "Can we guarantee latency for users in Europe/APAC?" -> "Yes — smart routing pins requests to regionally deployed runtimes and offers Dedicated pools with SLA-backed latency targets."
- "We need an air-gapped option." -> "We offer Private (VPC or on-prem) with the same API surface and the ability to keep traffic on your network."

Pricing language snippets (for different contexts):
- Website headline (concise): "Pay per inference. Predictable performance. Enterprise options for committed capacity."
- Pricing summary (customer-facing page): "Pay-as-you-go: $X per 1K tokens for generation (volume discounts available). Dedicated commitments: contact sales for reserved throughput and predictable monthly billing. Private deployments: licensing + support."
- In-console tooltip (on route config): "Route quota caps monthly token usage and prevents runaway bills — set a soft limit and notification email."
- First-contact email line: "Start with free developer credits, spin up a model in minutes, and see exact per-route token costs in the console."

Concrete quickstart checklist (developer flow):
- Sign up -> copy API key (free credit applied)
- Create route -> pick model variant -> set soft quota (e.g., 500K tokens/mo)
- Run sample call (paste test prompt) -> check tokens + latency in metrics
- Turn on prefix caching for chat/history-heavy routes
- If predictable load: request Dedicated estimate or trial

Competitive notes (short bullets — internal):
- Public cloud managed endpoints: they expose hardware but require you to tune and manage batching. Our advantage: built-in runtime batching + caching and model-variant fallbacks that keep apps online when the primary model is constrained.
- LLM API aggregators: competing for simplicity, but they often obscure cost and performance tradeoffs. Our UI surfaces token economics and latency tradeoffs per-route.
- Self-hosted runtime vendors: strong on control, weaker on packaged developer experience. Redwood’s value is the consistent API + ability to move to Private without rewriting code.

Acceptance signals (what to watch for in demo/product usage):
- Team creates >1 route with quotas set (shows they care about unit economics)
- They request prefix caching turned on or ask about caching behavior (history-heavy apps)
- Ask for Dedicated or estimate — signals scale intent and price sensitivity

Suggested A/B microcopy tests (first 500 users):
- A: "Start free — deploy an LLM feature in minutes. Pay-as-you-go, volume discounts."
- B: "From prototype to SLA — low-latency inference, per-route cost controls, and reserved capacity for scale."
Metric: activation-to-first-successful-inference time, then percent who set a quota.

Callouts for product team (implementation asks):
- Show a simple cost-estimator inline when a user creates a route: pick model, expected avg tokens, monthly estimate.
- Make the first quota creation step explicit in the route wizard (prevent surprises).
- Add a 'demo snapshot' button that runs the 90s demo flow with sample prompts for common verticals (search vs summarization vs chat).

Open questions / unresolved items (notes-to-self):
- What initial per-1k token public price do we land on for the website? Need finance input and competitive benchmark (action: loop in finance FY24-Q4).
- Which three model variants do we use for the in-console demo snapshot? Propose: small fast variant, balanced variant, high-quality variant.
- Measure: create a baseline report showing median tokens-per-inference for three sample workloads to inform price framing.

Quick outreach templates (short):
- Slack/DM to engineer: "Hi — want to try Redwood for a quick infer test? I can spin a demo route with free credits; you’ll see latency and per-route token numbers right away."
- Short email to platform lead: "We help teams move from PoC to SLA with predictable latency and committed capacity. Can I show a 5-minute demo this week?"

Next steps for this doc:
- Iterate with Finance on concrete price points and volume discounts.
- Build the demo snapshot and embed cost-estimator UX.
- Run an A/B test for microcopy A vs B across signup flow and track quota creation metric.

Notes: keep language concrete and engineer-oriented. Avoid generic marketing platitudes (e.g., 'AI for everyone') in early eval outreach — technical buyers respond to explicit outcomes (latency percentiles, cost per 1k tokens, caching behavior).

End of sprint-zero kit.
